business_problem: Lockheed Martin needed its PAC-3 MSE air and missile defense system to keep pace with evolving and emerging threats by increasing decision speed, improving decision quality, and adapting target engagement behavior in real time.
solution_summary: Lockheed Martin describes PAC-3 MSE as an in-house AI/ML-enabled interceptor capability rather than a cloud-based stack. The operational system is the PAC-3 MSE itself, which contains an embedded AI software component that Lockheed Martin says has existed in every fielded PAC-3 interceptor since the program’s inception. Within the engagement workflow, advanced fire control and battle management functions use AI to analyze battlespace data at high speed, improving decision speed and decision quality across detection, tracking, and target engagement. The implementation is positioned as spanning the kill chain so the interceptor can adapt to new threat behavior in real time while a threat is still airborne. The source does not identify a separate storage platform, external data source, or third-party integration layer; instead, it presents a tightly embedded, onboard AI decision stack inside the missile-defense system.
products_used: advanced fire control and battle management functions

solution_components.name: PAC-3 MSE
solution_components.role: The interceptor platform whose capability is being evolved with AI/ML to improve detection, tracking, engagement, and in-flight adaptation against advanced threats.

solution_components.name: embedded AI software component
solution_components.role: The onboard AI component inside PAC-3 interceptors that supports threat analysis and decision-making.

solution_components.name: advanced fire control and battle management functions
solution_components.role: The control layer that uses AI to analyze data and make rapid engagement decisions across the kill chain.

data_flow: Threat data enters the PAC-3 MSE engagement stack, where the embedded AI software component and AI-enabled fire control and battle management functions analyze it across the kill chain. The system uses those results to detect, track, and engage targets, then adapts its response in real time as threat behavior changes while the threat is still in the air.
business_outcome: Lockheed Martin says the AI-enabled PAC-3 MSE improves precision and speed in detecting, tracking, and engaging targets, adapts to new threat behavior in real time, and increases overall mission capability and battlefield awareness for warfighters.
